name: Ahmad Jamal
hook: A jazz pianist famous for space and restraint, whose playing became a favourite source for hip-hop producers.

blurb.age7: A jazz piano player. A piece of one of his songs was used in a famous Nas song.
blurb.age13: Ahmad Jamal was born in Pittsburgh in 1930 and became one of the most admired jazz pianists of his time. He was known for leaving space: playing fewer notes and letting silence do some of the work. Miles Davis said he learned from him. Pete Rock sampled Jamal's 'I Love Music' for Nas's 'The World Is Yours' in 1994, and many other producers have used his records. He died in 2023, aged 92.
blurb.adult: Jamal's aesthetic of space and repetition suits the loop, which is one reason hip-hop producers return to him. Miles Davis's regard for him is well documented in Davis's own accounts. Jazz is a roots lane on this map, traced only where a documented connection reaches later music, so Jamal is here as a sample hub (Q21).
